SCGSim prepares Palace and Ansys AEDT simulations of superconducting-chip
layouts and reads their results back. It began as a downstream derivation of
[gsim](https://github.com/gdsfactory/gsim) and now keeps its own geometry
builder, solver adapters and result readers.

## Scope {#scope}

SCGSim computes with Palace Electrostatic and Eigenmode, and with AEDT HFSS
Eigenmode, HFSS Driven Terminal, Q3D and Q2D;
[Supported calculations](../reference/supported-calculations.qmd) lists the
input and the returned quantity of each. Palace Driven, Magnetostatic and
Transient are not implemented, and Meep is outside the scope. The public
component notebooks belong to OrcaPen SC PDK.

SCGSim does not install a native solver, does not run a prepared handoff on
its own, and does not treat a result as accurate because the calculation
completed: the study's author chooses the physical assumptions and interprets
the quantities.

## Where SCGSim came from {#starting-source-identities}

| Origin | Version | Revision |
|---|---|---|
| gsim, downstream release | `0.2.0+scq.1` | `8f5dc6c05255d003a9c6d8959537bcf8068379d3` |
| The historical semantic geometry builder (SGB) | | `e74a343154c6b19b6ba32d6fb297e700cfe08ff2` |

These identities record where the code was derived from, nothing more. SCGSim
imports neither, falls back to neither and promises no API compatibility with
them: geometry is built by the in-tree `scgsim.geometry.sgb`.
